newsitem.title: USA: Starbucks to sell Oprah's Book Club selections.
newsitem.headline: Starbucks to sell Oprah's Book Club selections.

text.p: Starbucks Corp. said Wednesday it will begin selling talk show host Oprah Winfrey's monthly book club selection in its 1,100 coffee bars to benefit the chain's new charitable foundation.

Since the popular television star started her on-air book club in September, each monthly selection has soared onto national bestseller lists, selling at least 1 million copies in the succeeding four weeks.
Winfrey will announce her next selection in mid-June, and the book will remain on sale at Starbucks stores into September, covering a summer hiatus for the talk show.
All profits from books sold at Starbucks will be funnelled into the Starbucks Foundation and used for local literacy projects in cities where the coffee company has its outlets.

The foundation was launched this year with a donation of $500,000 by Starbucks Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Howard Schultz, who said he expected net profits from Oprah's Book Club to at least match that figure over the next year.

"I am pleased to support Starbucks in its efforts to improve literacy," Winfrey said in a statement. "One of the greatest pleasures in my life is reading. I believe books open windows to the world for all of us."

Schultz said in an interview that book sales were a "natural extension" for Starbucks, which has launched a successful line of music tapes and compact disks. He said he would not rule out the possibility the chain will expand its book sales.
One book that definitely will be offered for sale at the stores is Schultz's own book on Starbucks, which will go on sale Sept. 2.
Profits from the Schultz book, "Pour Your Heart Into It," also will benefit the foundation.
